questions.q: A triangle has sides 10 cm, 24 cm and 26 cm. Which conclusion follows from the converse of Pythagoras theorem?
options: A) It is right-angled, with 26 cm as hypotenuse
D) It cannot form a triangle
questions.answer: A) It is right-angled, with 26 cm as hypotenuse
questions.explanation: The largest side is 26 cm. We have 10^2 + 24^2 = 100 + 576 = 676, and 26^2 = 676. Since the square of the largest side equals the sum of the squares of the other two, the triangle is right-angled with hypotenuse 26 cm.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have areas 36 cm^2 and 100 cm^2. If a side of the larger triangle is 20 cm, what is the corresponding side of the smaller triangle?
questions.explanation: For similar triangles, the ratio of areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides. Thus smaller side / larger side = sqrt(36/100) = 6/10. The required side is 20 x 6/10 = 12 cm.

questions.q: A 15 m tower casts a 24 m shadow while, at the same instant, a pole casts a 16 m shadow. Assuming the Sun rays make the same angle with the ground, what is the pole height?
questions.explanation: The tower and pole form right triangles with equal acute angles made by the Sun rays, so the triangles are similar by AA. Hence height/shadow is the same for both: 15/24 = h/16. Solving gives h = 15 x 16 / 24 = 10 m.

questions.q: In a right triangle ABC right-angled at B, altitude BD meets hypotenuse AC at D. If AD = 4 cm and DC = 5 cm, which pair is correct?
options: A) BD = 3 cm and AB = 6 cm
B) BD = 2sqrt(5) cm and AB = 3sqrt(5) cm
C) BD = sqrt(20) cm and AB = sqrt(20) cm
D) BD = 2sqrt(5) cm and AB = 6 cm
questions.answer: D) BD = 2sqrt(5) cm and AB = 6 cm
questions.explanation: The altitude-to-hypotenuse similarity relations give BD^2 = AD x DC = 4 x 5 = 20, so BD = 2sqrt(5). Also AC = 4 + 5 = 9 and AB^2 = AD x AC = 4 x 9 = 36. Therefore AB = 6 cm.
